parallel.requirements: The prompt exposed 84 named Jenkins requirements and required every file under /workspace/requirements to be read and implemented.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parallel configuration enabled multi-agent mode, but no spawn, child path, child activity, or ownership assignment executed before failure.
parallel.implementation: No implementation work occurred; cell metadata records zero tool calls, zero LLM requests, and no requirement patches were collected.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No patch integration or deliverable assembly happened, and final.txt contains no final response from the failed turn.
parallel.verification: The agent performed no local verification; the official harness later ran run-tests.sh and reported failure on the uncompleted solution.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: All 84 requirements remained unfinished according to outer loop progress, and the official evaluation marked the solution failed.

serial.requirements: The serial run used the same 84-requirement prompt and harness progress updates to keep working through remaining slugs.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Serial mode disabled multi-agent execution; a single agent owned requirement reading, implementation, patch generation, and follow-up rounds.
serial.implementation: The agent produced partial implementation commits and requirement patch files, with harness counts rising from 22 to 36 to 40 collected patches.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Serial integrated a subset of changes into the local workspace and committed per-requirement patches, but left many requirements incomplete.
serial.verification: The official harness ran direct run-tests.sh after the third round; it exited with status 1 and reported the final failed tests.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Serial still had only 40 of 84 requirements credited and failed 53 final test identifiers, so the partial implementation did not resolve the task.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The prompt required reading all 84 requirement files and implementing every change, but the parallel attempt did not progress past startup.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial attempt received the same requirement list and used the repeated harness progress state to continue working through requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel recognized only the prompt surface before failure; serial processed the task enough for the harness to credit 40 completed requirement patches.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Multi-agent mode was enabled in configuration, but protocol validation recorded no spawn calls, child paths, or child activity.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial mode explicitly disabled multi-agent features and executed all work in one local agent across three rounds.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel attempt had no executed ownership split; the serial control had single-agent ownership and therefore no delegation boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: No child briefs, handoffs, or interface contracts were created because the turn failed before any delegation or task work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child context transfer; it carried state through harness progress and local workspace continuation across rounds.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no parallel context-boundary defect to compare; serial context movement was ordinary single-agent continuation rather than inter-agent transfer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel attempt made no implementation edits and produced no requirement patch collection before tests ran on the initial or effectively unchanged tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial attempt created a sequence of requirement patches, reaching 22, then 36, then 40 collected patch files before final testing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial produced partial implementation artifacts while parallel produced none; both were still insufficient for a passing official run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The only parallel trajectory events are thread start, turn start, stream reconnect errors, and turn failure; no child result or final answer exists.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial rounds timed out, but the outer loop consumed each round enough to collect progressively more requirement patch files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had no result lifecycle beyond process failure; serial had partial local results collected between timed-out rounds.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Because no child ran and no edits were made, there were no parallel shared-workspace writes, collisions, overwrites, or integrations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked in one shared local workspace and accumulated committed requirement patches, with implementation conflicts and incomplete integration remaining ordinary local defects.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The paired contrast does not show a parallel merge or shared-state coordination error; it shows absent parallel work versus partial serial integration work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel agent performed no in-trajectory verification; the official harness later ran tests and reported failure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial work was followed by the official direct test run, which exited with status 1 and reported the same failed final test set.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither produced passing acceptance evidence; serial at least reached a testable partial implementation, while parallel did not verify agent-created work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel exited after about 13 seconds with return code 1, zero LLM requests, zero tokens, and zero tool calls.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial spent three timed-out rounds, accumulating 632 LLM requests and 1150 tool calls in cell metadata before official failure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closed almost immediately due to an agent error; serial consumed the available rounds on implementation work but still left more than half the requirements incomplete.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both modes failed the current completed official evaluation. The main task-solving difference is that parallel-mode execution never actually used the enabled multi-agent mechanism or produced work, while serial execution made partial single-agent progress through 40 requirement patches before tests failed. This explains process coverage differences, not a discordant official outcome.
parallel_contributors: The parallel Codex turn failed on stream disconnection before performing any task work.
Protocol validation recorded zero spawn calls, zero child paths, and zero child activity, so no parallel coordination mechanism executed.
No final answer or implementation artifacts were produced by the parallel agent before official testing.
serial_contributors: The serial control ran three non-delegated timed-out rounds and accumulated partial requirement patch coverage.
The harness collected 40 requirement patch files from serial before the final direct test run failed.
Serial still left 44 of 84 requirements uncredited, so its partial implementation was insufficient.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial shows ordinary long-task implementation incompleteness and integration defects; those are not parallel coordination taxonomy events.
Parallel shows an agent/process stream failure rather than a coding or merge defect inside child-agent work.
evaluator_effects: No evaluator asymmetry was observed; both official evaluations completed under the same task id and reported the same failed final test identifiers.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported comparative explanation of process differences
